addedLines: - claude: Catch-all for any task that doesn't fit a more specific agent. FleetView's default when no agent name is typed. (Tools: *)

- Explore: Fast read-only search agent for locating code. Use it to find files by pattern (eg. "src/components/**/*.tsx"), grep for symbols or keywords (eg. "API endpoints"), or answer "where is X defined / which files reference Y." Do NOT use it for code review, design-doc auditing, cross-file consistency checks, or open-ended analysis — it reads excerpts rather than whole files and will miss content past its read window. When calling, specify search breadth: "quick" for a single targeted lookup, "medium" for moderate exploration, or "very thorough" to search across multiple locations and naming conventions. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- general-purpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries use this agent to perform the search for you. (Tools: *)

- Plan: Software architect agent for designing implementation plans. Use this when you need to plan the implementation strategy for a task. Returns step-by-step plans, identifies critical files, and considers architectural trade-offs. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)
- statusline-setup: Use this agent to configure the user's Claude Code status line setting. (Tools: Read, Edit)

attachment.content:
- gitnexus-cli: Use when the user needs to run GitNexus CLI commands like analyze/index a repo, check status, clean the index, generate a wiki, or list indexed repos. Examples: "Index this repo", "Reanalyze the codebase", "Generate a wiki"
- gitnexus-debugging: Use when the user is debugging a bug, tracing an error, or asking why something fails. Examples: "Why is X failing?", "Where does this error come from?", "Trace this bug"
- gitnexus-exploring: Use when the user asks how code works, wants to understand architecture, trace execution flows, or explore unfamiliar parts of the codebase. Examples: "How does X work?", "What calls this function?", "Show me the auth flow"
- gitnexus-guide: Use when the user asks about GitNexus itself — available tools, how to query the knowledge graph, MCP resources, graph schema, or workflow reference. Examples: "What GitNexus tools are available?", "How do I use GitNexus?"
- gitnexus-impact-analysis: Use when the user wants to know what will break if they change something, or needs safety analysis before editing code. Examples: "Is it safe to change X?", "What depends on this?", "What will break?"
- gitnexus-pdg-query: Use when querying or extending GitNexus's PDG control/data-dependence surface (the `pdg_query` MCP tool, CDG/REACHING_DEF edges), or reasoning about "what controls X" / "where does Y flow" / guard clauses. Examples: "what guards this statement?", "trace this variable within the function", "why is the pdg_query result empty?", "add a CDG query".
- gitnexus-pr-review: Use when the user wants to review a pull request, understand what a PR changes, assess risk of merging, or check for missing test coverage. Examples: "Review this PR", "What does PR #42 change?", "Is this PR safe to merge?"
- gitnexus-refactoring: Use when the user wants to rename, extract, split, move, or restructure code safely. Examples: "Rename this function", "Extract this into a module", "Refactor this class", "Move this to a separate file"
- gitnexus-taint-analysis: Use when working on, reviewing, or extending GitNexus's CFG/taint/PDG subsystem (the `--pdg` layers), or when reasoning about source→sink data-flow findings. Examples: "How does taint analysis work here?", "Why didn't explain find this flow?", "Add a new sink/source", "Review the interprocedural taint code".
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo, defaults to 10m) - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- review: Review a GitHub pull request; for your working diff use /code-review
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

content.text:
Now I have a comprehensive picture. Here is my full report.

---

## Server-Side Memo Visibility Enforcement Sites

Below is every distinct enforcement site where memo visibility is checked or filtered on the server side, organized by file.

---

### 1. Central Read-Access Guard: `checkMemoReadAccess`

**File:** `/bench/home/work/server/router/api/v1/memo_service.go` (lines 39-68)

This is the primary reusable gate for single-memo read access. It enforces two rules:
- **Archived memos** are only visible to their creator.
- **Non-PUBLIC memos** require authentication. **PRIVATE memos** are denied to anyone except the creator.

PROTECTED memos are implicitly allowed for any authenticated user (no explicit deny for them).

**Callers:**
- `GetMemo` (line 356) -- also checks the parent memo at line 367 when the memo is a comment.
- `ListMemoComments` (line 148 in `memo_service_comments.go`) -- gates reading a memo's comment list.

---

### 2. ListMemos Visibility Filtering

**File:** `/bench/home/work/server/router/api/v1/memo_service.go` (lines 218-227)

When listing memos, visibility is enforced at the **query level** (database filter), not per-row post-fetch:
- **Anonymous user (nil):** `VisibilityList` is set to `[PUBLIC]` only.
- **Authenticated user viewing all creators:** a CEL filter is appended: `creator_id == <self> || visibility in ["PUBLIC", "PROTECTED"]`. This lets the user see their own private memos plus all public/protected memos.
- **Authenticated user viewing a specific other user:** `VisibilityList` is set to `[PUBLIC, PROTECTED]`.

---

### 3. CreateMemoComment Visibility Check

**File:** `/bench/home/work/server/router/api/v1/memo_service_comments.go` (lines 33-43)

Before allowing a user to create a comment on a memo, the parent memo's visibility is checked:
- If the parent memo is PRIVATE and the user is not its creator (and not admin), the request is denied.

Additionally, at line 52, the comment's own visibility is **forced** to match the parent memo's visibility.

At line 100, if the comment is not PRIVATE and the commenter is not the parent creator, an inbox notification is created -- this is a visibility-aware notification decision, not an enforcement per se.

---

### 4. ListMemoComments Visibility Filtering

**File:** `/bench/home/work/server/router/api/v1/memo_service_comments.go` (lines 148, 157-161)

First calls `checkMemoReadAccess` on the parent memo (line 148). Then applies a visibility filter to the comments themselves:
- **Anonymous:** `visibility == "PUBLIC"`.
- **Authenticated:** `creator_id == <self> || visibility in ["PUBLIC", "PROTECTED"]`.

---

### 5. ListMemoReactions Visibility Check

**File:** `/bench/home/work/server/router/api/v1/reaction_service.go` (lines 29-41)

Before listing reactions for a memo:
- If the memo is not PUBLIC, authentication is required.
- If the memo is PRIVATE and the user is not the creator and not an admin, access is denied.

---

### 6. UpsertMemoReaction Visibility Check

**File:** `/bench/home/work/server/router/api/v1/reaction_service.go` (lines 82-85)

Before allowing a reaction on a memo:
- If the memo is PRIVATE and the user is not the creator and not an admin, the request is denied.

---

### 7. ListMemoAttachments Visibility Check

**File:** `/bench/home/work/server/router/api/v1/memo_attachment_service.go` (lines 213-225)

Before listing attachments for a memo:
- If the memo is not PUBLIC, authentication is required.
- If the memo is PRIVATE and the user is not the creator and not an admin, access is denied.

---

### 8. GetAttachment / `checkAttachmentAccess` (API layer)

**File:** `/bench/home/work/server/router/api/v1/attachment_service.go` (lines 255-258 calling; lines 419-455 implementing)

The `checkAttachmentAccess` method enforces visibility on attachment reads through the API:
- **Unlinked attachments** (no memo): only the creator or admin can access.
- **Linked attachments**: the linked memo's visibility rules apply:
  - PUBLIC memo: anyone can access.
  - Non-PUBLIC memo: authentication required.
  - PRIVATE memo: only the creator or admin can access.

---

### 9. FileServer `checkAttachmentPermission` (file serving layer)

**File:** `/bench/home/work/server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go` (lines 649-704, called at line 149)

This is the file-serving counterpart. It runs on the `/file/...` endpoint (Echo handler, not gRPC). The logic is richer than the API-layer check:
- **Unlinked attachments:** creator or admin only.
- **PUBLIC memo + anonymous-access instance:** served to anyone (line 677).
- **Share token fallback** (lines 684-688): if the request carries a valid, non-expired share token for the specific memo, access is granted regardless of visibility.
- **Authenticated user:** if the memo is PRIVATE, only the creator or admin can access (line 699).

---

### 10. ListMemoRelations Visibility Filtering

**File:** `/bench/home/work/server/router/api/v1/memo_relation_service.go` (lines 107-112)

When listing relations for a memo, a visibility filter is applied to the *related* memos:
- **Anonymous:** `visibility == "PUBLIC"`.
- **Authenticated:** `creator_id == <self> || visibility in ["PUBLIC", "PROTECTED"]`.

This ensures that a user cannot discover the existence of related private memos they do not own.

---

### 11. Batch Relation Loading (`batchConvertMemoRelations`)

**File:** `/bench/home/work/server/router/api/v1/memo_service_converter.go` (lines 173-206)

When batch-loading relations for multiple memos (used during `ListMemos`, `ListMemoComments`, etc.), the same visibility filter is applied:
- **Anonymous:** `visibility == "PUBLIC"`.
- **Authenticated:** `creator_id == <self> || visibility in ["PUBLIC", "PROTECTED"]`.

---

### 12. GetUserStats Visibility Filtering

**File:** `/bench/home/work/server/router/api/v1/user_service_stats.go` (lines 217-221)

When computing a single user's stats:
- **Anonymous:** `VisibilityList = [PUBLIC]`.
- **Authenticated user viewing another user:** `VisibilityList = [PUBLIC, PROTECTED]`.
- **Authenticated user viewing self:** no visibility restriction (sees all including PRIVATE).

---

### 13. ListAllUserStats Visibility Filtering

**File:** `/bench/home/work/server/router/api/v1/user_service_stats.go` (lines 83-91)

When computing stats across all users:
- **Anonymous:** `VisibilityList = [PUBLIC]`.
- **Authenticated, all creators:** CEL filter `creator_id == <self> || visibility in ["PUBLIC", "PROTECTED"]`.
- **Authenticated, specific other user:** `VisibilityList = [PUBLIC, PROTECTED]`.

---

### 14. SSE Hub Event Delivery Filtering (`canReceive`)

**File:** `/bench/home/work/server/router/api/v1/sse_hub.go` (lines 134-144)

The Server-Sent Events hub filters which clients receive which events based on the memo's visibility:
- **PRIVATE:** only the creator's SSE connection (matched by `userID`) or an admin receives the event.
- **PUBLIC, PROTECTED, or empty visibility:** all connected clients receive the event.
- **Unknown visibility:** denied (logged as warning).

---

### 15. RSS Feed: Global and Per-User

**File:** `/bench/home/work/server/router/rss/rss.go` (lines 90, 141)

Both the global RSS feed and the per-user RSS feed restrict output to PUBLIC memos only:
- `VisibilityList: []store.Visibility{store.Public}`

---

### 16. Sitemap Generation

**File:** `/bench/home/work/server/router/frontend/frontend.go` (line 150)

The sitemap XML generation only includes PUBLIC memos:
- `VisibilityList: []store.Visibility{store.Public}`

---

### 17. Mention Notification Visibility Guards

**File:** `/bench/home/work/server/router/api/v1/memo_mention_helpers.go` (lines 56-89)

The functions `canUserAccessMentionContext` and `shouldSkipMentionInbox` check visibility before sending @-mention notifications:
- `canUserAccessMentionContext` (line 56): if the related memo is PRIVATE and the target user is not its creator, returns false. Same for the memo itself.
- `shouldSkipMentionInbox` (line 74): calls `canUserAccessMentionContext` and skips inbox creation if the target cannot access the context. Also skips duplicate notification when a comment on a non-PRIVATE memo already triggers a comment inbox item (line 84).

---

### 18. Comment Visibility Inheritance on Update

**File:** `/bench/home/work/server/router/api/v1/memo_service.go` (lines 452-464)

When a memo's visibility is updated, if the memo is a comment (has a `ParentUID`), its visibility is **forced to match the parent memo's visibility**, overriding whatever was requested. This ensures a comment cannot be made more visible than its parent.

---

### 19. GetMemoByShare (Share Token Access)

**File:** `/bench/home/work/server/router/api/v1/memo_share_service.go` (lines 153-192)

The `GetMemoByShare` endpoint bypasses normal visibility checks entirely -- it uses a share token to grant access. No authentication is required. However, it still checks that the memo is not archived (line 164), treating archived/missing memos as invalid tokens to avoid information leakage.

---

### 20. ACL Configuration (Public Method List)

**File:** `/bench/home/work/server/router/api/v1/acl_config.go` (lines 32-41)

The `PublicMethods` map declares which RPC endpoints are accessible without authentication. The memo-related public endpoints are:
- `GetMemo`, `ListMemos`, `ListMemoComments`, `GetLinkMetadata`, `BatchGetLinkMetadata`, `GetMemoByShare`

The comment at line 32 explicitly notes: "visibility filtering done in service layer." This means the ACL layer lets anonymous requests through, and the service-layer code (sites 1-4 above) performs the actual visibility enforcement.

---

### 21. Authorizer (`CheckAccess`)

**File:** `/bench/home/work/server/router/api/v1/authz.go` (lines 58-69)

The `Authorizer.CheckAccess` method is the gateway interceptor that decides whether an anonymous request reaches the service layer at all. For private instances (no InstanceURL), only `AuthBootstrapMethods` and first-run `CreateUser` are allowed -- effectively blocking anonymous access to memo endpoints even though they are in `PublicMethods`.

---

### 22. Database Layer: Visibility Filtering in Store Drivers

**Files:**
- `/bench/home/work/store/db/sqlite/memo.go` (lines 96-102)
- `/bench/home/work/store/db/mysql/memo.go` (lines 104-110)
- `/bench/home/work/store/db/postgres/memo.go` (lines 89-95)

All three database drivers (SQLite, MySQL, PostgreSQL) translate `FindMemo.VisibilityList` into a SQL `WHERE memo.visibility IN (...)` clause. This is the low-level enforcement that makes the service-layer visibility settings (sites 2, 12, 13, 15, 16) effective at the database query level.

---

### 23. Filter Schema: Visibility as Filterable Field

**File:** `/bench/home/work/internal/filter/schema.go` (lines 162-172)

The CEL filter schema registers `visibility` as a filterable field (mapped to `memo.visibility` column), supporting `==` and `!=` operators. This enables the CEL filter expressions used in sites 2, 4, 10, 11, and 13 (e.g., `visibility in ["PUBLIC", "PROTECTED"]`).

---

### Summary Table

| # | File | Function/Site | What it enforces |
|---|------|--------------|-----------------|
| 1 | `memo_service.go:39` | `checkMemoReadAccess` | Central single-memo gate: archived creator-only; PRIVATE creator-only; non-PUBLIC requires auth |
| 2 | `memo_service.go:218` | `ListMemos` | Query-level visibility filter by auth state |
| 3 | `memo_service_comments.go:41` | `CreateMemoComment` | PRIVATE parent memo blocks non-creator commenters |
| 4 | `memo_service_comments.go:148,157` | `ListMemoComments` | Read-access check on parent + visibility filter on comments |
| 5 | `reaction_service.go:29` | `ListMemoReactions` | Visibility check before listing reactions |
| 6 | `reaction_service.go:82` | `UpsertMemoReaction` | PRIVATE memo blocks non-creator/non-admin reactions |
| 7 | `memo_attachment_service.go:213` | `ListMemoAttachments` | Visibility check before listing memo attachments |
| 8 | `attachment_service.go:419` | `checkAttachmentAccess` | API-layer attachment access via memo visibility |
| 9 | `fileserver.go:649` | `checkAttachmentPermission` | File-serving layer: memo visibility + share-token fallback |
| 10 | `memo_relation_service.go:107` | `ListMemoRelations` | Visibility filter on related memos |
| 11 | `memo_service_converter.go:173` | `batchConvertMemoRelations` | Batch visibility filter on related memos |
| 12 | `user_service_stats.go:217` | `GetUserStats` | Visibility filter for per-user stats |
| 13 | `user_service_stats.go:83` | `ListAllUserStats` | Visibility filter for all-user stats |
| 14 | `sse_hub.go:134` | `canReceive` | SSE event delivery filtering by visibility |
| 15 | `rss.go:90,141` | RSS feeds | PUBLIC-only memos in feeds |
| 16 | `frontend.go:150` | Sitemap | PUBLIC-only memos in sitemap |
| 17 | `memo_mention_helpers.go:56` | `canUserAccessMentionContext` | Blocks mention notifications for PRIVATE memos to non-creators |
| 18 | `memo_service.go:452` | `UpdateMemo` visibility path | Forces comment visibility to match parent |
| 19 | `memo_share_service.go:153` | `GetMemoByShare` | Share-token bypass (no visibility check, archived blocked) |
| 20 | `acl_config.go:11` | `PublicMethods` | Declares memo endpoints as publicly routable (defers to service layer) |
| 21 | `authz.go:58` | `Authorizer.CheckAccess` | Gateway-level anonymous-access policy for private instances |
| 22 | `store/db/*/memo.go` | DB drivers | SQL `WHERE visibility IN (...)` clause generation |
| 23 | `internal/filter/schema.go:162` | Filter schema | Enables `visibility` as CEL-filterable field |
